chunks: And from him, from Salamah ibn Muhammad, who said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Mudarrab narrated to us from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from al-Haytham al-Nahdi, from Ali ibn Asbat, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I said to him: Indeed, Allah begins by looking at the visitors of the grave of al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him) on the evening of 'Arafah before He looks at the people of the standing (at 'Arafah). He said: 'Yes.' I said: 'And how is that?' He said: 'Because among those (visitors) are the children of fornication, and among these (people of 'Arafah) are not the children of fornication.'

key_terms.أَوْلَادَ زِنًى: Children of fornication (born out of wedlock)

ai.seo_question: Why does Allah look at visitors of Imam Husayn's grave before the pilgrims at 'Arafah?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the unique spiritual status of Ziyarat al-Husayn by contrasting the grave visitors with the pilgrims at Mount Arafat. The Imam’s reasoning—that grave visitors include 'children of fornication' (those born out of wedlock) while the Arafat pilgrims do not—suggests that the merit of Ziyarat extends to a broader, more inclusive demographic, offering redemption to those with varied social and familial backgrounds. This underscores the universal accessibility of Imam al-Husayn’s shrine as a place of divine favor regardless of lineage purity.
